newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Thin Australian stocks climb to record close.
newsitem.headline: Thin Australian stocks climb to record close.

text.p: A thinly traded Australian share market climbed to a record close on Monday with a combination of end-of-year window-dressing and futures-led trading providing most of the impetus.
The All Ordinaries index added 17.3 points to 2,412.9 after reaching a record intraday high of 2,416.8, surpassing the previous high of 2,408.9 set on November 26.
"It looks like a bit of positive post-Christmas cheer," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding that while trade was thin in the Christmas-New Year hiatus, the rises had been widespread.
"There has been no action in the market turnover. It's certainly not busy but most of the rises are across the board."
Other players echoed these sentiments, adding that the December futures contract's retention of a modest premium augured well for Tuesday's expiry.
"It's pushed ahead rather than raced ahead but the futures look to have a lock on the premium and that should help the market hold tomorrow," said a Sydney broker.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
